- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often over-estimates continuation; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending up, model frequently under-reacts; add 0.5–1.5 price point bias to forecast.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast should be slightly below; if below, slightly above.
- For 30-day horizon, model often over-predicts early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at +2% above recent 7-day high.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment rises, forecast should rise; if sentiment falls, forecast should fall).
